races.name: Ampion Electrical Testing And Solar Experts Nursery Handicap

runners_data.name: Bit Of A Buzz
runners_data.note: Consistent each-way performer with four placings from five starts, all at 5f, and Gavin Cromwell's yard is firing at 2/45 over the past fortnight; the unclassified style means this filly could slot anywhere in the field and her willingness to compete makes her adaptable to the likely sprint-finish shape
runners_data.comment: Third last time out and fourth in three of his last five starts, without a win in that spell but competitive throughout. Last seen 15 days ago and proven over today's trip, he leads our figures by a wide margin - the yard's recent slump the one reservation.

runners_data.name: Shafters Legacy
runners_data.note: Worrying tendency to fade in the closing stages is a serious concern in a race that is almost certain to become a sprint finish; the 28-day break and a single placing from three attempts on comparable ground suggest Andrew Slattery will need things to fall perfectly here
runners_data.comment: Third last time out after modest efforts before that - unplaced two starts back, and eighth prior - she sits bottom of our figures here. She does have experience over today's trip, but a yard well out of form adds to the concerns.

runners_data.name: Tatianna
runners_data.note: Josh Halley's filly has only three career starts and a best of third on soft ground at 5f, showing modest form on good going to date; her hold-up style means she needs something to race against, and with no true front runner here her finishing kick may find little to aim at
runners_data.comment: Modest of late - sixth last time out, seventh before that, but she was third three starts back and still ranks third of our five on figures. Last seen 23 days ago with experience over today's trip, though she needs to rediscover that level to be a threat.

runners_data.name: Santorini Storm
runners_data.note: JP Murtagh's charge returns after a 69-day break and has been below expectations in all three career starts, beaten a long way each time; a true hold-up type at heart, Ben Coen is likely to find this horse in a more forward position than suits, competing for space with others of similar inclination
runners_data.comment: A slowly improving formline - fifth last time out having been sixth and seventh before that - hints at more to come, and he ranks fourth of our five on figures. The concern is a 69-day absence since that run, leaving fitness the obvious doubt.

runners_data.name: Mr Montauk
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's juvenile has Dylan Browne McMonagle booked, which is a significant jockey upgrade angle worth noting after a 59-day absence; however, this is a genuine hold-up horse placed by circumstance into a midfield role in a race with no pace to chase, and three starts without a placing on good ground tempers the optimism
runners_data.comment: Modest of late - unplaced last time out after seventh and fifth before that - but he's up to second of our five on figures, well clear of his official mark, with the yard in good form. A 59-day absence is the concern.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front runner in a five-runner field over five furlongs at Down Royal, this race is likely to begin at a moderate tempo as horses feel their way forward, before developing into a sprint finish from the two-furlong pole. Bit Of A Buzz is the only runner with an unclassified (U) style that could drift forward, but absent a genuine pace-setter, the race shape is dictated by default — a contested but not truly fast gallop that compresses the field and blunts any significant positional advantage. The entire field is effectively composed of hold-up and midfield types, meaning the outcome hinges on who quickens best from a bunched, relatively sedate early pace rather than who survives a punishing front-running display. This shape marginally favours runners with a sharp turn of foot who can exploit the sprint finish, rather than those needing cover and a strong pace to aim at — Bit Of A Buzz, as the sole horse with any forward tendency, is best placed to dictate if connections choose to commit early. The field holds more genuine hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear, with Santorini Storm and Mr Montauk redistributed into midfield slots — both Ben Coen and Dylan Browne McMonagle are likely to find themselves closer than ideal with little natural pace ahead to stalk.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the field settles into a steady-to-moderate gallop and the race becomes a flat-out dash from two furlongs out
scenarios.body: Without a genuine front runner to stretch the field, runners bunch together and the sprint finish rewards the horse with the sharpest acceleration; Bit Of A Buzz, with forward tendencies and a consistent form string, is positioned to benefit from dictating a comfortable early rhythm

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Bit Of A Buzz Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Bit Of A Buzz is allowed to stride forward uncontested and sets a controlled front-running tempo
scenarios.body: A solo lead at a manageable pace over five furlongs on good ground allows the leader to conserve energy and kick clear inside the final furlong; Gavin Cromwell's two-year-olds have strong recent form and Ellie Gartlan's claim makes this combination well-equipped to exploit a leadership vacuum

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely quick enough to create a meaningful finishing kick from the rear
scenarios.body: Tatianna or Shafters Legacy, tracking midfield, would need a true pace to run at — on good ground over five furlongs with no confirmed front runner, that scenario is unlikely to fully materialise; the redistribution of Santorini Storm and Mr Montauk into midfield further muddles the genuine hold-up angles, making this shape harder to execute

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart Chaotically
scenarios.trigger: If multiple runners jostle for position in the early stages creating an uneven, stop-start gallop
scenarios.body: A messy pace scenario can produce unexpected results as horses are shuffled out of rhythm; Mr Montauk, with Dylan Browne McMonagle in the saddle and Joseph O'Brien's backing, possesses the class to recover from a troubled passage better than most in this field

watchPoints.text: Bit Of A Buzz is the only horse in this field with any plausible claim to the front, and if Ellie Gartlan commits early and secures an uncontested lead, the rest of the field — composed entirely of hold-up and midfield types — will have nothing to race against

Santorini Storm and Mr Montauk are both true hold-up horses likely to be forced closer than ideal; watch for both jockeys negotiating an uncomfortable early position, which could compromise their runs and cause interference heading into the sprint

Shafters Legacy's flagged tendency to fade in the finish is a specific red flag in a race almost certain to resolve as a sprint — Jimmy Dalton will need to be creative to counter a pattern that has appeared consistently

The entire field is unproven over multiple starts at this track; with the going listed as unknown and Down Royal's going report blank across all runners, surface variability is an added unknown that could disproportionately affect pace readings in the early stages

races.name: Ampion Electrical Testing And Solar Experts Handicap

runners_data.name: Bye Bye Now
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who has been tactically placed out of her natural role here according to the style tag, but recent win at 5f on Good (2nd in sim-going records only partially tells the story) makes her the key pace influence; sole lead horse in the race gives her a tactical gift, though the STYLE_FIT flag is worth noting if conditions change.
runners_data.comment: Second last time out, and a winner three starts back, she's yet to finish outside the frame across that five-race sequence and ranks fourth of our twelve on figures. Last seen 14 days ago with experience over today's trip, though the yard is currently out of form.

runners_data.name: Shamanka
runners_data.note: Tongue-tie and a poor recent record at this trip and beyond (17th and 13th in last two starts) makes her hard to back confidently; true hold-up type who needs a strong pace to close into, which this race shape is unlikely to provide, and the 28-day break is no particular positive with a cold trainer stat.
runners_data.comment: Fourth last time out after two unplaced efforts, but she tops our figures for this field and rates the one to beat. Last seen 28 days ago with experience over today's trip, though she's without a win in that sequence - the one blot.

runners_data.name: Viamonte
runners_data.note: Has been placed at 5f on Good going four times in recent history, showing genuine course-trip competence, but is a true hold-up horse who will be seeking a pace that may not materialise; Adam Browne-Souza takes a 7lb claim which helps at the weights, and the p headgear suggests a degree of consistency.
runners_data.comment: Fourth last time out after two unplaced efforts, and he is yet to win in that recent sequence. He ranks second of our twelve on rating and was last seen 14 days ago, with experience over today's trip - the finishing sequence the one query against him.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Eagles
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on Good and placed twice on soft at the course, showing this ground does not worry him; a proper hold-up type who ideally wants a gallop to aim at, and while the 16-day return is fine, his best chance depends on pace scenario C unfolding.
runners_data.comment: Eighth last time out was below her best, but that followed a third and, three starts back, a win - form that puts her third of our twelve on figures. Last seen 16 days ago with experience over today's trip, though last time's flop is the query.

runners_data.name: Raven's Call
runners_data.note: 282-day absence is a serious flag — this 3yo has only three career runs and a best of 5th, and Edward Lynam's T14 stat of 1/4 is not strong enough to inspire confidence on a comeback; the ⚠ fades-in-finish warning compounds the concern for a horse who needs things to fall perfectly.
runners_data.comment: A lengthy 282-day absence compounds modest form figures - ninth last time out, fifth and unplaced before that - and she's down among the tail of our twelve on rating. Experience over today's trip is the one thing in her favour, but she has plenty to find.

runners_data.name: Hot To Foxtrot
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with three placings on Good ground at the trip, and Ronan Whelan is the obvious upgrade at this level; at OR=52 he is competitive off this mark and his 28-day break is acceptable, making him one of the more straightforward pace-shape beneficiaries if he tracks the leader throughout.
runners_data.comment: Modest recent form - sixth last time out, with a third two starts back the best of it, which leaves her fifth of our twelve on rating, squarely midfield. Last seen 28 days ago with experience over today's trip, but she is yet to win in that sequence.

runners_data.name: Practical Move
runners_data.note: Long absence of 185 days is a major concern and the recent form string of 9650-9 is discouraging; a genuine hold-up horse who has been mapped to midfield due to overcrowding at the rear, meaning his natural late-running style is further compromised — the combination of absence and positional difficulty makes this a tough assignment.
runners_data.comment: Modest form figures - ninth last time out and no better than midfield before that - and a 185-day absence adds a fitness query. She has experience over today's trip and sits sixth of our twelve on rating, but there's little here to inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Whatswrongnow
runners_data.note: Six-day turnaround for a horse with four placings from nine starts on Good ground suggests connections are happy with his current state; Dylan Browne McMonagle is a significant jockey booking, and his prominent style slots perfectly into the pace map without any redistribution complication.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out continues a fairly consistent if winless sequence that has also produced a second, and he's quickly back in action just six days on. He sits ninth of our twelve on rating though, leaving him more to find than most.

runners_data.name: Dandy Land
runners_data.note: Unclassified style adds unpredictability but a Good-ground placing at 5f is in the book, and Willie McCreery's T14 of 2/18 shows the stable is sending out winners; tongue-tie (v) could help sharpen him up, and W J Lee's experience in tight finishes makes him relevant if the race bunches.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out was her best in a run of otherwise modest efforts, and she sits seventh of our twelve on rating - firmly midfield. Last seen 14 days ago with experience over today's trip, but she needs to build on that placing to feature.

runners_data.name: Spirit Above
runners_data.note: Placed at 5f on Good going and ran 2nd over 5f in a similar race recently — the underlying form is there; however, this is a genuine hold-up horse shifted into midfield by the crowded rear, meaning his finishing kick may be wasted if he cannot get back to his true position, and the 6-day return has produced a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93.
runners_data.comment: Unplaced last time out, though a fourth and, before that, a second show he retains some ability on his day. Back in action just six days on, he sits eighth of our twelve on rating - modest form leaves him with work to do to feature.

runners_data.name: Monastere
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on Good going and placed at the trip, so the form credentials are legitimate, but the ⚠ fades-in-finish warning combined with being a true hold-up horse displaced to midfield creates a double-layered concern; 6-day turnaround keeps him fresh, but getting a clear run on this pace map will be difficult.
runners_data.comment: Fifth last time out, though that came after a win two starts back, and a second before that, so there's ability there, but he sits bottom of our twelve on rating. Back in action just six days on is the one thing in his favour.

runners_data.name: Snowballs
runners_data.note: Lowest rated runner in the field at OR=44 with a form string of 787859 that shows no meaningful threat in recent Good-ground sprints; a true hold-up type bumped to midfield, carrying the weakest STYLE_FIT score in the field alongside Practical Move — this combination of low ability and positional compromise makes it hard to build a case.
runners_data.comment: A modest recent sequence - ninth last time out, and no better than fifth before that - leaves him eleventh of our twelve on rating. Back in action six days on with experience over today's trip, but there's little here to inspire confidence.

races.paceDynamic: Bye Bye Now is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner 5f handicap and, with no genuine pace rival likely to push for the lead, she can dictate at a controlled, sustainable tempo from the outset. Hot To Foxtrot and Whatswrongnow are the most natural prominent horses to track her, with Dandy Land's unpredictable style adding a degree of uncertainty to the early order. A lone pace-setter setting a measured gallop on Good ground over a sharp five furlongs creates a classic scenario where the lead horse conserves enough energy to repel challengers late, favouring those who race on or close to the pace rather than those forced to make up ground from deep. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Practical Move, Spirit Above, Monastere and Snowballs are all genuine closers but at least some will be bumped forward into midfield positions that compromise their natural game; of those, Spirit Above and Monastere are most likely to actually secure closer-to-pace berths given recent form activity. The tactical verdict is clear: a comfortably-paced lead dictated by Bye Bye Now benefits prominent racers who can sit within a length or two of the front and pounce, rather than true hold-up horses who need a strong gallop to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bye Bye Now Controls Wire-To-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Bye Bye Now is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and the pace proves steady enough that her stamina holds over the final furlong.
scenarios.body: She sets a comfortable tempo, her rivals never quite get organised to close the gap, and the Good ground suits her form profile at the trip; those tracking closely like Hot To Foxtrot and Whatswrongnow are the only threats in the final 100 yards.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Bye Bye Now shows early then begins to tie up inside the final furlong and one or both of the prominent trackers capitalise with a sustained run.
scenarios.body: Whatswrongnow and Hot To Foxtrot, sitting within a couple of lengths throughout, find the most ground when the pace eases and their consistent Good-ground form comes to the fore; this shape rewards horses who have shown ability to hit the line in similar conditions rather than relying on a strong pace to close from behind.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow and creates a wall of horses in the final furlong, allowing one of the repositioned closers to find a late gap.
scenarios.body: Spirit Of Eagles or Monastere, both capable on Good ground at the trip and carrying competitive form, could benefit if sufficient daylight opens up late; however, this shape is structurally weakened by the fact that several of the true hold-up types have been pushed forward, meaning fewer genuine closers are positioned to deliver a true late run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Bunches, Melee Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the sedate pace causes a compression of the field turning for home and the result is decided by a tight, chaotic finish between multiple horses.
scenarios.body: Dandy Land's versatile style and W J Lee's positional intelligence could prove decisive in a scrappy finish, while Shamanka at a big price might find the race coming back to her from off the pace; this scenario is the least structured but cannot be entirely dismissed given the low-grade nature of the field and the compressed weights.

watchPoints.text: Bye Bye Now controls the pace entirely alone — watch if she is allowed to stride clear unchallenged in the first two furlongs, as a soft lead at this trip on Good ground can be very difficult to peg back.

Whatswrongnow's booking of Dylan Browne McMonagle is a stable flag — watch for any market move at the off, as this combination has the profile to land a touch in a low-grade handicap with a clear pace map in front of them.

Raven's Call returns after 282 days with only three career runs and a fades-in-finish flag — watch her behaviour in the parade ring and early in the race, as a slow jumper or a reluctant traveller would confirm she is best opposed.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses (Monastere, Spirit Above, Practical Move, Snowballs) creates positional pressure in the early stages — watch for interference or checking in the first two furlongs as genuine closers bump into each other trying to find their natural ground.

Hot To Foxtrot at 6d turnaround has performed to a placed level at this trip and going on multiple occasions — watch his early positioning under Ronan Whelan, as getting on the heels of Bye Bye Now immediately would put him in the ideal tactical spot for this race shape.

races.name: Ampion Electrical Testing And Solar Experts Maiden
GAIN The Advantage Series Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Banana Three
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter here — Shane Markey's 7lb claim helps the welter burden somewhat, and her three placings at similar distances on good ground indicate she handles the conditions, though her recent form string (5375) is modest and she races as a prominent type tasked with leading alone today, which tempers confidence in her ability to score rather than simply shape the race.
runners_data.comment: Fifth last time out and fifth in three of his last five starts, yet he tops our figures in this seven-runner race. Last seen 21 days ago with experience over today's trip, though he remains without a win in that spell.

runners_data.name: Booklight
runners_data.note: Jimmy Dalton (4lb claim) partners this four-year-old who showed placed form at 12f on good ground, and at 35 days between runs freshness could help — she is a genuine prominent racer likely to contest the early position behind Banana Three, and her step up in trip to 1m5f is the key stamina question to resolve.
runners_data.comment: Unplaced last time out, though that followed a third two starts back, and a fourth three starts back, she holds solid claims as second of our seven on figures. Last seen 35 days ago with experience over today's trip, though she needs to bounce back from that below-par run.

runners_data.name: Memories Maker
runners_data.note: 381 days off the track is the dominant concern here — Anthony McCann's yard has shown no recent form (0/6 T14) and this hold-up operator has struggled to place on good ground in recent starts, with her best efforts coming over a shorter trip, making the combination of a long absence and this test a significant ask.
runners_data.comment: A serious fitness query surrounds a 381-day absence. Unplaced last time out, which came after a fifth two starts back, and a second three starts back, form that puts him fourth of our seven on figures - though that lengthy a break makes him hard to trust fully fit.

runners_data.name: Rising Sky
runners_data.note: Back quickly after just 6 days — a flag worth noting — and carries hood and tongue-tie headgear as a prominent runner who has placed twice at similar trips on good going; Adam Grant's 7lb claim helps but the rapid turnaround and a moderate form record (0W) suggest this is a horse in active search of a race that fits rather than one in peak form.
runners_data.comment: Seventh last time out was below-par, but she landed one six starts back and shows ability in between with a third, form that puts her third of our seven on figures. Back in action just six days on with experience over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Numidia
runners_data.note: Won at 14f on good going as recently as 15 days ago, which is the most relevant positive piece of form in the field — Mel Sheridan takes the ride, and while this horse is naturally a front-runner by instinct, the crowded early positions in this race mean she is likely to settle further back than ideal, so the extent to which she can reproduce that winning effort from an unaccustomed position is the key uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Landed his latest start, a much-needed change of fortune after a run of modest efforts, and he was last seen 15 days ago with experience over today's trip. Fifth of our seven on figures, the question is whether that upturn can be sustained.

runners_data.name: Searcog
runners_data.note: Patrick Magee's yard is in fine form (T14: 4/11) and Julian Pietropaolo's 2lb claim is useful — Searcog has placed form at 16f on good ground and represents a genuine hold-up runner with proven stamina at this sort of trip; the 83-day gap is a mild concern but the trainer's current strike rate lends confidence the horse arrives ready.
runners_data.comment: The form has faded across this sequence - a win and a second earlier in it, but two fourths followed by an eighth last time out. An 83-day gap since that flop compounds the concerns, and she sits sixth of our seven on figures.

runners_data.name: Masego
runners_data.note: Won at 13f on good ground and has placed three times in recent starts, showing solid form at staying trips — John McConnell's yard has been quiet of late (0/42 T14) which is a significant red flag, and while Masego is a true hold-up horse by nature, the modest trainer form and a race shape unlikely to produce the strong pace he needs to close into dampens his prospects here.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, though that came after a win two starts back, so there's encouragement there, but he's bottom of our seven on figures and the yard is currently out of form. He does have experience over today's trip and was last seen 14 days ago.

races.paceDynamic: Banana Three is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger likely to press from the outside, she should be able to control tempo at a measured, sustainable clip over this 1m5f trip. The field does contain more prominent-minded horses than the race shape can accommodate — Numidia and Masego are both natural forward-goers who have been redistributed rearward on the map, and in reality Booklight and Rising Sky will also be competing for early position, meaning the early order could be fractionally busier than a lone-leader scenario implies. Nevertheless, Banana Three's ability to dictate at her own tempo, dictating fractions without a true pace rival on her shoulder, creates a controlled, steadily-run contest that is unlikely to produce a significant late sprint. This shape — a modest, front-controlled gallop over a staying trip — strongly favours prominent-to-midfield horses with proven stamina and the ability to travel smoothly just off a solo leader, rather than true closers who need a genuine pace to chase down.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Banana Three Controls Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Banana Three leads uncontested and sets a sustainable, even gallop that suits prominent chasers.
scenarios.body: Banana Three dictates fractions without pressure, ensuring the race develops at a tempo she can handle, and horses that track her neatly within two lengths have first run entering the straight. Prominent types who can travel efficiently just off the pace are the primary beneficiaries, as the winner is most likely to emerge from the chasing pack rather than from further back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens Mid-Race
scenarios.trigger: If the cluster of prominent runners — Booklight, Rising Sky — push forward and apply unexpected pressure on Banana Three from the outset.
scenarios.body: A contested early gallop stretches the field and raises the overall tempo, exposing the front-runner and tiring midfield horses that lack resolution at the trip. Horses with proven stamina at the distance and the tactical ability to settle just off a genuine pace before challenging have the clearest path here.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Finish Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final quarter-mile, leaving the field bunched and enabling rear-ward runners to swoop.
scenarios.body: A very slow early tempo causes compression entering the straight, and horses held up toward the back find more daylight than usual in a small seven-runner field. However, Masego and Searcog — the genuine hold-up types here — would need an uncharacteristically strong late-race kick from a flat-race pace, which is a lower-probability outcome.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Stolen Win
scenarios.trigger: If Banana Three is never seriously challenged and gallops rivals into submission with an uncontested front-running display.
scenarios.body: With no rival capable of sitting on her shoulder throughout, Banana Three is allowed to control every yard at a pace that suits her stamina profile, and the chasers find themselves unable to close the gap in time once the straight is reached. This outcome is dampened by her recent form and the OR ceiling she carries relative to her rivals.

watchPoints.text: Numidia's winning form at 14f just 15 days ago is the standout data point in the race — watch whether Mel Sheridan can secure a position closer to the pace than the map suggests, because if she gets cover in third or fourth she becomes a serious threat to the scenario winners.

Booklight and Rising Sky will both want to sit prominently behind Banana Three, and if they push forward aggressively in the early stages there is a risk of an unplanned mid-race acceleration that blows the race wide open and compromises the front-runner.

Memories Maker has not run for 381 days and McCann's yard has produced no winners from six runners in the last 14 days — treat any market move for this horse with caution as the fitness question is unresolved and there is no fitness evidence to support backing her at odds.

Searcog's trainer Patrick Magee is the form trainer in this field (4/11 T14) — even at the lowest OR in the field, track this runner in the betting as a lightly-weighted hold-up type with the most in-form yard represented.

Masego's connections (0/42 T14) represent a stark trainer form warning that should weigh against his otherwise reasonable recent form figures when assessing his chance of winning rather than merely filling a place.

races.name: Ampion Electrical Testing And Solar Experts Fillies Handicap

runners_data.name: Stellar Quality
runners_data.note: Prominent runner by style with a win at 12f on good ground in recent form; Keithen Kennedy's 5lb claim is a live asset in a small field, and four of five profile runs on similar going show two wins and two places — ideally suited to tracking a lone leader here.
runners_data.comment: Stellar Quality's form reads 6th-3rd-5th-1st-3rd, winning four starts back, and she has raced over today's trip before. Rated 91 to an 81 official mark, she's the one to beat, though a yard out of form and 25 days off may be a mild concern.

runners_data.name: Beauparc
runners_data.note: Colin Keane booked for this six-year-old who has been running in shorter races at 10f — the step back up to 1m5f looks overdue given a placed effort at 12f on good ground, but the trainer's recent 0/7 strike rate over 14 days asks questions of current stable form.
runners_data.comment: Beauparc was a solid second three starts back and has form at today's trip; rated 89 off an 80 mark, she's right in this. She's without a win in her last six starts though, with each of her last two runs a below-par 6th.

runners_data.name: Alba Chiara
runners_data.note: Won over 18f so stamina is not the issue here, but three consecutive zeros including two finishes of 16th and 19th at 14f on good ground are alarming; Wayne Lordan takes the ride but form profile gives little encouragement in a race where positional ground-loss from a rear draw will be hard to recover.
runners_data.comment: A winner five starts back, and second next time, with today's trip already proven. Our figures rate her a good deal above her official mark, though three unplaced runs since are the clear risk after 27 days off.

runners_data.name: Teologia
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with a 0.90 style-fit flag, meaning it is being asked to lead here rather than race from a more natural handy position — the O'Brien yard has had a strong recent 14-day strike rate of 20/56, and Teologia's two recent wins suggest current fitness, making it the key pace influence despite the role adjustment.
runners_data.comment: Teologia arrives on two straight wins, with a second three starts back and a yard in good current form. But our rating of 80 sits below her 84 mark, and a modest 66 speed figure is the concern after 27 days off.

runners_data.name: La Dame Blanche
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse by record — four of its last five runs show mid-pack to rear tracking — but redistributed to midfield in the pace map as the field's rear is already occupied by other true closers; at OR 65 it is the lowest-rated runner, and the style-fit tag (0.91) underlines the structural difficulty of getting its ideal position in a five-runner field.
runners_data.comment: La Dame Blanche is the lowest of this five on our figures, without a win in her last five starts and no better than 4th in that run. Her 74 speed figure and a rating of 77 - well above her 65 mark - hint at underused ability, with today's trip already proven.

races.paceDynamic: Teologia is the confirmed pace-setter and, in a field of just five, will lead from the front without meaningful pressure — Stellar Quality is the only other runner likely to race prominently, tracking just off the early leader, while Beauparc, Alba Chiara, and La Dame Blanche are all hold-up types that will be ridden from off the pace over this 1m5f trip. With Teologia able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop unchallenged, the tempo is unlikely to be truly searching, which historically favours those who can travel close to the pace rather than deep closers who need a strong end-to-end gallop to close ground. This shape tilts the race in favour of prominent and close-tracking runners who can respond to any quickening in the straight without having excess ground to make up. The field does hold more genuine hold-up types than the pace map can place at the rear — La Dame Blanche is a true hold-up horse that has been mapped to midfield to reflect the crowded rear, but is unlikely to be in a natural position and its chance in any shape relying on late sweep should be discounted accordingly.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Teologia Controls, Tracks Win
scenarios.trigger: If Teologia dictates a modest, uncontested gallop and Stellar Quality tracks throughout to pounce.
scenarios.body: Teologia sets the fractions from the front and, with no rival willing to push the pace, controls the race from start to finish; Stellar Quality, racing prominently in second, is ideally positioned to challenge off a false gallop in the straight and poses the primary threat.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Grind Down Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely strong enough that hold-up horses can reel in the leaders in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A stronger-than-expected gallop from Teologia stretches the field and creates enough of a true test that Beauparc or Alba Chiara can generate momentum from off the pace; Beauparc's class and Colin Keane's positional intelligence would be key assets in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Seizes It Late
scenarios.trigger: If Stellar Quality is produced with a well-timed challenge and Teologia's front-running effort finds a limit in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Stellar Quality's recent form and experience at longer trips on good ground suggests it can sustain a run through the final furlong if the pace has been modest; the combination of a pace-collapse scenario and a tactically sharp Keithen Kennedy ride makes this a plausible alternative outcome.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If La Dame Blanche or Alba Chiara overcome their positional disadvantage and the race develops into a genuine staying test.
scenarios.body: La Dame Blanche's redistribution from the rear to midfield reflects that it is unlikely to secure a true hold-up berth, making a late swooping run structurally difficult from the outset; Alba Chiara won over 18f and has the stamina, but its recent string of zeros and a style-fit mismatch make this a low-probability outcome.

watchPoints.text: Watch Teologia's early stride pattern — if Dylan Browne McMonagle is able to slide across unchallenged and find a comfortable rhythm within the first two furlongs, the race is effectively over as a tactical contest and the front two set the terms throughout.

Monitor Stellar Quality's position at the first bend — if Keithen Kennedy can slot into second without expending energy, the prominent profile becomes the most tactically advantaged in the race; if it gets shuffled back, the chance changes shape entirely.
Beauparc's trip up from 10f races is a key variable — if the 1m5f trip does not prove its optimum, Colin Keane may be forced to commit earlier than ideal, which could compromise the hold-up plan.

Alba Chiara's recent form figures of 0-0-0 warrant monitoring in the paddock — any sign of lack of enthusiasm or coat condition would further undermine an already unconvincing recent profile over this course type.

La Dame Blanche has run just 10 days ago and carries headgear — watch whether it settles cleanly in what will be a slowly-run early tempo, as a hold-up horse in a dawdling race with no room at the rear faces a compounding positional problem.

races.name: Ampion Electrical Testing And Solar Experts Handicap

runners_data.name: Leeward
runners_data.note: Carries a "fades in finish" flag which is a significant concern in a sprint-style finish at 1m5f; Ben Coen's booking is the one positive angle but the form string of 9780 offers no encouragement and similar-going returns show 0 wins from 4 starts.
runners_data.comment: Leeward's recent form reads a subdued unplaced, 8th, 7th and 9th, but he still ranks second of seven in this field on our figures. He carries 140 lb and hasn't run for 37 days, with a modest 60 speed figure the concern.

runners_data.name: Sea Of Dubka
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes the ride for Henry De Bromhead and that pairing is the headline angle here — has placed at 1m2f-1m4f on good ground and steps up in trip, which could unlock further stamina; 60-day absence worth noting.
runners_data.comment: Sea Of Dubka ran a fair third three starts back and has form over today's trip, though her last two runs (4th, then 5th) mark a step back. Away for 60 days, without a win in five and a modest rating of 63, she needs more to fully convince.

runners_data.name: Glen Echo
runners_data.note: Carries a "fades in finish" concern and four consecutive poor finishes on good ground make the form bleak — operates naturally at the rear but is mapped to midfield here as this field has too many hold-up horses, meaning it will likely find itself further forward than ideal, which suits its fade profile least.
runners_data.comment: Glen Echo's last four reads unplaced, unplaced, 7th and unplaced, and the yard is out of form at just 2% over the last 14 days. He does have experience over today's trip and a 68 speed figure well above a modest rating of 61, hinting at more in the tank.

runners_data.name: Chapel Island
runners_data.note: Headgear (tongue-tie) fitted and was last seen just 13 days ago, suggesting connections are pressing for a quick return; a natural closer whose redistribution into midfield could inadvertently place it in the ideal position should the pace develop slowly, giving it a slight positional edge over the true back-markers.
runners_data.comment: Chapel Island's form has improved with each of his last three starts, down to a 4th last time. A rating of 76 makes him clear best of this seven, well up on a modest 59 mark, and despite being without a win in five, a fresh 13-day turnaround makes him the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Onyeisi
runners_data.note: Blinkers fitted and trainer Karl Thornton has a quiet 14-day strike rate (0/4) — the form reads 270740 with four runs on good ground and poor returns; like several others it is a true hold-up horse shuffled into a midfield slot, and the style fit of 0.91 reflects real risk of racing out of role.
runners_data.comment: Onyeisi's finishing positions have dipped since a 2nd the longest way back, with unplaced, 4th, 7th and unplaced since, though a rating of 63 - well clear of a 55 mark - still keeps him third-best in this seven. 25 days off may freshen him up, but that recent form is the concern.

runners_data.name: Augusta Rock
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle is the standout jockey booking in this field and the Joseph Patrick O'Brien yard is in excellent 14-day form (20/56) — the blinkers suggest a behavioural angle and the horse ran just four days ago, which is extremely quick; the "fades in finish" tag is the main concern, but connections clearly believe it is in form.
runners_data.comment: Augusta Rock is rated bottom of this seven, with only a 5th last time out from a run that also includes two 8ths. He does have a quick turnaround (4 days since his last run) and joins a yard currently in strong form, 35% over the last 14 days.

runners_data.name: Nephin Mountain
runners_data.note: Wesley Joyce (3lb claim) takes the mount and the form string 404840 over sprint trips suggests this 1m5f assignment is a significant step up in distance for a horse that has barely threatened in nine similar-going starts; the "fades in finish" flag is doubly damaging at this longer trip.
runners_data.comment: Nephin Mountain has hit 4th three times in his last six starts but was unplaced last time, a mixed recent picture. A rating of 62, clear of a 51 mark, keeps him mid-pack in this seven, with a modest 58 speed figure and 13 days since his last run.

races.paceDynamic: This is an all-hold-up field over 1m5f at Down Royal, with every single runner carrying a genuine rear-to-midfield style and not one confirmed front-runner to set the tempo — the race is likely to crawl early before erupting into a sprint-style dash in the final two furlongs. Sea Of Dubka, Glen Echo, and Chapel Island have the better recent form at similar trips, and whoever summons the most finishing kick from a tardy gallop will dictate the result. The field contains more hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear, meaning Glen Echo, Chapel Island, Onyeisi, Augusta Rock, and Nephin Mountain are all redistributed into midfield slots despite being natural closers — none of them will get a true sit-and-sprint position, and whoever idles closest to the pace by accident may be best placed of all. This race shape strongly favours any runner that can travel comfortably in mid-division and produce a sustained, rather than a sharp, finishing effort, as a truly muddling gallop will expose those who fade late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Messy Crawl, Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the field idles at a pedestrian early pace and the race becomes a bunched cavalry charge from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: With no genuine front-runner, the pace will be set reluctantly and the final two furlongs will be everything — runners who travel smoothly in midfield and quicken off a slow tempo hold the clear edge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Runner Grabs Modest Lead
scenarios.trigger: If a rider takes a calculated decision to pop to the front and dictate an uncontested moderate gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: A solo horse controlling terms over 1m5f on good ground could prove very difficult to peg back, particularly if the hold-up brigade sit too far back in a slow-run contest.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Storm Late From Rear
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop quickens meaningfully mid-race and genuine stamina becomes the deciding factor in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: A stronger pace would stretch the field and allow true staying types to run through beaten horses in the final furlong — though most of this field carry the "fades in finish" tag, limiting the pool of genuine beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Jockey Tactics Decide
scenarios.trigger: If one rider makes a decisive positional move turning for home that the rest of the field cannot react to in time.
scenarios.body: Colin Keane on Sea Of Dubka or Dylan Browne McMonagle on Augusta Rock represent the highest-profile tactical riding threats in this otherwise evenly matched field — a well-timed run from the widest angle could catch rivals flat-footed.

watchPoints.text: Augusta Rock ran just four days ago — monitor markets for late drifting or withdrawal, and watch whether Dylan Browne McMonagle attempts to take a lead from the front given there is no natural pace-setter in this field.

Glen Echo, Chapel Island, Onyeisi, Augusta Rock and Nephin Mountain are all true hold-up horses redistributed into midfield on the map — watch for a chaotic, bunched early-race scenario with riders jostling for positions they cannot all occupy.
Sea Of Dubka returns after 60 days off for Henry De Bromhead — watch the market move; if Colin Keane has had a spin at home the stable confidence may be reflected in significant support.

With no front-runner confirmed, watch whether any jockey makes a bold decision to exploit the pace vacuum by leading from flag-fall — whoever does so from this field could secure a significant positional advantage at almost no cost.
Nephin Mountain's 1m5f trip is the longest it has ever attempted based on its history of 7f-9f runs — watch for it to be outpaced as soon as the field quickens in the closing stages.
